Dynatec Madagascar SA Announces Major Investment to Expand Mining Operations

ANTANANARIVO, Madagascar, June 14 — Dynatec Madagascar SA, a leading player in the country’s metals and mining sector, announced Thursday it will move forward with a significant investment to expand its nickel and cobalt operations in the Atsinanana region. The project, expected to total $250 million over the next two years, aims to increase annual production capacity by 30%, according to company officials.

"This expansion underscores our long-term commitment to Madagascar and to the ongoing development of sustainable mining practices," said Jean-Claude Rakotoarisoa, Dynatec Madagascar SA’s General Manager. "We anticipate the new facilities will create up to 400 direct jobs during the construction phase and an additional 150 permanent roles once operations begin."

The planned investment will fund the construction of new processing facilities and the modernization of existing infrastructure at the Ambatovy site. The company also plans to implement enhanced water management systems and introduce advanced ore refining technologies designed to reduce environmental impact.

Industry analysts say the move positions Dynatec Madagascar SA to better meet rising global demand for battery metals. "With the increasing shift toward electric vehicles and renewable energy storage, demand for nickel and cobalt is only expected to grow," said Liva Ramanantsoa, a mining sector analyst at the Madagascar Mineral Resources Institute. "This expansion could significantly boost Madagascar’s export revenues and reinforce the country’s standing in the global supply chain."

The expansion is being carried out in close coordination with local authorities and community leaders. The company has pledged to maintain its focus on community engagement, including investments in local infrastructure, education, and health initiatives.

The Madagascar Mining Workers’ Union welcomed the announcement. "We are encouraged by the company’s commitment to job creation and skills development for Malagasy workers," said union spokesperson Fanja Razafindrainibe.

Construction is scheduled to begin in September, with the expanded facilities expected to become operational by late 2026. Dynatec Madagascar SA has operated in the country for more than a decade, with its flagship project among Madagascar’s largest foreign investments.
